req.title: Create requires title
req.statement: The system shall render 'Title is required.' when POST /create omits the title field.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-016 requires that POST /create returns HTTP 2xx and renders 'Title is required.' when the title field is omitted. Three test cases are designed: (1) Positive — authenticated user POSTs with a valid title and body, expects redirect (302) and no error message, confirming the happy path works and the validation branch is not triggered. (2) Negative — authenticated user POSTs with title omitted entirely (key absent), expects 200 and 'Title is required.' in response body, directly testing the requirement. (3) Boundary — authenticated user POSTs with title as empty string (the exact boundary between absent and present), expects 200 and 'Title is required.' in response body, catching off-by-one or truthiness mutations on the `if not title` guard. Each test sets up its own in-process Flask app with a temp database, registers and logs in a user, then exercises the endpoint.

tests.name: test_create_with_valid_title_succeeds
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
User 'Rahul' registered and logged in (session active)
actions: POST /create with title='Valid Title' and body='Some body text'
expected: Response does NOT contain 'Title is required.'
trace: R-FLASKR-016: positive path — title present, no validation error expected
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

# Register and login
client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
r_login = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
assert r_login.status_code == 302

# POST /create with valid title
r = client.post('/create', data={'title': 'Valid Title', 'body': 'Some body text'})
assert r.status_code == 302
assert b'Title is required.' not in r.data

os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_create_with_empty_string_title_shows_error
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
User 'Ishaan' registered and logged in (session active)
actions: POST /create with title='' (empty string) and body='Some body'
expected: Response body contains exactly 'Title is required.'
trace: R-FLASKR-016: boundary — empty string title is falsy, triggers same validation as absent title; catches mutations on `if not title` (e.g. `if title` or `if title is None`)
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

# Register and login
client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'Ishaan', 'password': 'stone'})
r_login = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Ishaan', 'password': 'stone'})
assert r_login.status_code == 302

# POST /create with empty string title (boundary: len==0)
r = client.post('/create', data={'title': '', 'body': 'Some body'})
assert r.status_code == 200
assert r.status_code != 302
assert b'Title is required.' in r.data

# Confirm single-char title does NOT trigger error (boundary+1)
r2 = client.post('/create', data={'title': 'A', 'body': 'Some body'})
assert r2.status_code == 302
assert b'Title is required.' not in r2.data

os.unlink(path)
